coverage.target: NFR1 (feed content displays within 2 seconds) is specifically FeedUnit's request path; ReminderUnit shares no request path with the feed's content-display flow
NFR3 (payment-data handling) belongs to donation-unit; ReminderUnit has no payment surface
NFR6.1 (services/-layer access boundary and mandatory self-review before merging guest-identity-authorization or event-handler-idempotency changes)
Accessibility (WCAG AA baseline) is a UI-rendering concern owned by flutter-app-unit; ReminderUnit has no UI of its own
Testing methodology/coverage floor is a cross-cutting Build and Test concern, not a Unit-level NFR target

note: performance-requirements.md (NFR-PERF.1-3), scalability-requirements.md (NFR-SC.1), observability-requirements.md (NFR-OBS.1-4), and security-requirements.md's NFR-AUTHZ.1 (guest-identity authorization model) and NFR-AUTHZ.2 (push-token registration abuse, accepted risk) are intentionally outside the NFR1-NFR8 inheritance chain above: inception's requirements.md defines no top-level authorization-model NFR (NFR3/NFR5 are payment-specific, NFR4 is data-protection, NFR6 is the access-boundary/process rule already correctly mapped to NFR6.1), and no performance/scalability/observability NFR for this Unit's own request paths, so all of these use Unit-local IDs rather than a fabricated inception sub-ID (added at this stage's review, R-03, which caught NFR-AUTHZ.1's earlier omission from this note). NFR-PERF.3 (push delivery timing) is notable as the one target in this project that constrains an as-yet-undecided Infrastructure Design mechanism rather than an already-built one.
